propositions: When two bundles exist for a single ref, git ls-remote returns the ref at two SHAs and a fresh clone fails with 'multiple updates for ref not allowed', making the store unclonable.
git-remote-s3's upstream Doctor.fix_multiple_bundles is interactive-only (blocking input() on EOF) and discards the non-chosen head's events, causing data loss in rebar's append-only event log.

The doctor must merge divergent bundle heads losslessly (reusing rebar's existing 2-parent git merge logic from sync._union_merge), never discard, and serialize repair via the helper's acquire_lock/release_lock.
The repair must write the merged bundle durably before deleting any originals and never delete the merged tip, ensuring at least one lossless bundle survives every crash point.

Detection of multi-bundle state via stderr signature in push.py must trigger a single auto-heal (guarded by healed_once) that folds N divergent heads via iterated 2-parent reconcile_one calls, then retry the push.

The optional s3_doctor.py module must route all S3 access (lock, enumerate, put, delete) through git-remote-s3's own S3Remote library and boto3 client, adding no direct S3 SDK or credential dependency to core rebar.
